title: Report memory usage the way the monitoring code does

blocks.text: The page's monitoring code reads each memory pool's `MemoryUsage` and prints it. A `MemoryUsage` has `init`, `used`, `committed` and `max`; **`max` is -1 when the pool has no defined maximum** (Metaspace, for one). *Committed* is what the JVM has reserved from the OS, *max* is the ceiling the pool may grow to.

items: `line(name, usage)`: `Pool [<name>]: used=<u>MB, max=<m>MB`, where sizes are **whole mebibytes** (bytes / 1,048,576, rounded down) and an undefined maximum prints as `max=-1MB`.
`usedPercent(usage)`: `100 * used / max` as an `OptionalDouble`, measured **against `max`**, and empty when `max` is undefined.

cases.says: A pool using 100 MiB of a 512 MiB maximum prints as Pool [G1 Old Gen]: used=100MB, max=512MB, and its usage is 19.53125 percent.
Sizes are divided by 1,048,576 and rounded down, so 1,572,863 bytes print as 1MB.
A pool whose maximum is undefined (-1) prints max=-1 and has no usage percentage.
The percentage divides used by the maximum, not by the committed size.

concepts: MemoryMXBean and MemoryPoolMXBean report used, committed and max for each area, and max is -1 when a pool has no limit.
